gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.title: JurassiCraft Field Guide
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.lore_hint: Turn the page for field notes on this species.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.introductio: This guide follows a fossil from the field to a living animal or ancient plant. Use it on a dinosaur to inspect its health, growth, sex, food and water.
Collect and clean fossils, grind them for tissue, then use laboratory machines to sequence, combine and synthesize DNA. Finally, grow an embryo or plant callus.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.fossils.lef: Use Plaster and Bandage on a dinosaur fossil block, then mine the encased fossil. Mine plant fossil blocks directly. Amber can also contain samples.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.fossils.rig: Put an encased fossil or plant fossil block in a Cleaning Station with water. Grind the resulting fossil bones, plant fossils or twigs for a chance of tissue.
Fossil nests can also be wrapped with Plaster and Bandage. Mine the wrapped nest and clean it with water to uncover fossilized eggs.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.nests.right: Put a fossilized egg in the Fossil Grinder. It may yield soft tissue from a prehistoric animal; other attempts produce flint or bone meal.
Put tissue and a blank Storage Disc in the DNA Sequencer to make a species-specific DNA disc. The sample's DNA quality is shown on the disc.
The DNA Extractor also accepts mosquito amber, aphid amber, sea lamprey or suitable dinosaur meat, together with a blank Storage Disc. Each can produce a DNA disc.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.synthesis.l: Use the DNA Combinator / Hybridizer to combine two discs of the same species and type. Their quality adds up to a maximum of 100%. Keep combining until you have a complete disc.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.synthesis.r: Put a 100% disc, an Empty Test Tube and DNA Base Material in the DNA Synthesizer. It produces a DNA tube and keeps the disc. Smelt a water bottle to make the base material.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.hatching.le: For an animal, put its DNA tube, a Petri Dish and an Empty Syringe in the Embryonic Machine. Put the resulting embryo syringe and a chicken egg in the Embryo Calcification Machine.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.hatching.ri: Place an egg and Peat Moss in an Incubator. Above 50 gives a male; 50 or below gives a female. Use the hatched egg on a block to release the animal.
Coelacanths grow in a Cultivator rather than a calcified egg. Insert the coelacanth embryo syringe and two water buckets. The machine returns the empty buckets.
Add food until each of the four nutrient bars is at least half full. Set temperature above 50 for a male or 50 and below for a female. Use the finished coelacanth in water to release it.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.plants.left: Use an Empty Syringe on a flower or other small plant to collect cells. Smelt gracilaria for Liquid Agar, then craft an agar Petri Dish and add plant cells.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.plants.righ: Put a plant DNA tube, Plant Cells Petri Dish and Empty Syringe in an Embryonic Machine to make callus. Use it on farmland; aquatic callus needs source water above suitable sediment.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.care.left.b: Feed hungry dinosaurs by hand. Meat-eaters eat meat; plant-eaters eat plants, leaves, saplings and seeds. Feeders can supply land animals.
Young carnivores and Gallimimus eat insects; Microraptors eat them at any age. Coelacanths eat fish, krill and plankton. Provide water and contain predators.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.orders.left: Some species imprint on the player who releases them from a hatched egg. Sneak while releasing one to keep it unimprinted.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.orders.righ: Use an empty hand on your imprinted dinosaur to choose wander, follow or stay. Sneak-use an empty hand on a mature owned animal to open its inventory.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.breeding.le: A healthy, well-fed and watered mature male and female of the same species can breed. Keep them together and give them space and time.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.breeding.ri: Land animals lay eggs that hatch after some time; use an egg to pick it up. Coelacanths give birth in water. Young inherit DNA from their parents.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.park.left.b: Join fence bases and place a pole above one. Power that base with redstone to electrify connected wires within eight blocks. Contact can shock animals and players.
Use a dart gun once to load up to twelve darts from your inventory, then use it again to fire. Tranquilizer darts put dinosaurs to sleep temporarily.
Use a vehicle item on solid ground, then use the vehicle to ride. The driver uses movement keys. In a helicopter, jump rises and sprint descends.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.tours.right: Lay connected tour rails on solid blocks. An Explorer placed on the route can follow them; the colored rails have different speeds.
Look for raptor paddocks and the visitor centre. Its rooms can contain the personal journals of the park staff, with entries to read and collect.
Use a fine net for small aquatic food, keep insects in a bug crate, and assemble fossil bones into skeleton displays. Place action figures as decorations.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.vel: Velociraptor was a small theropod dinosaur that lived in East Asia during the Late Cretaceous. An opportunist, it hunted a wide variety of prey ranging from small mammals and lizards, to medium-sized dinosaurs. Quick, highly intelligent, and highly aggressive, Velociraptor is very hard to keep. They accomplished escape artists, and have a good memory. They rival a cheetah's speed, and can leap up to 4 metres vertically.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.coe: Coelacanths are the last modern Coelocanthiform fish, an order dating back to the Devonian. The word "coelacanth" means "hollow spine". Using 8 different fins, the coelacanth can easily turn in almost any direction. Coelacanths are nocturnal, piscivorous drift-hunters found only in the depths of the Indian Ocean. Prehistoric coelacanths however were hugely diverse. Coelacanths are oviviviparous.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.mic: One of the most famous feathered dinosaurs ever found, Microraptor lived in northeast China during the Early Cretaceous. Microraptor's feathers are known to have been iridescent black. Microraptor is an intelligent pack-hunting predator that eats insects and other small animals.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.bra: Brachiosaurus was a giant sauropod that lived in North America. It can grow up to 25 or 26 metres long and 9 metres or more in height, and can weigh up to 40 tons. It is thought to have browsed from the tops of trees, eating mostly ginkgo leaves, conifers, tree-ferns, and large cycads. Brachiosaurs live in herds of 2 - 15 individuals, led by an alpha male or female. They produce trumpeting "singing" calls to communicate with one another.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.mus: Mussaurus is a small prosauropod dinosaur from Triassic Argentina. Its name means "mouse lizard", as for a long time it was known only from tiny baby skeletons. The proportions of the babies suggest the adults cared for them. Mussaurus are very small for sauropodomorphs, and are relatively easy herbivores to take care of. All they need is lush vegetation, some trees, and water.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.dil: At 6-7 metres long, this Early Jurassic theropod from Arizona was one of the first large predatory dinosaurs. It had twin crests on its head that may have been for sexual display. Dilophosaurus is actually venomous, preferring to spit venom into its prey's eyes. If the venom hits the eyes, it causes blindness and agonizing pain, and eventually paralysis. Dilophosaurus lives in small, disorganized gangs (around 3 - 10 individuals) of both males and females.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.gal: Gallimimus was a herbivorous theropod that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous. It measured 6 - 8 m when fully grown. It preferred to live near water, grazing on vegetation and sifting algae. Gallimimus was a fast runner, although its top speed is currently unknown. Gallis are herding animals that live in flocks of 10 - 100 individuals, usually a mix of males and females. They are extremely panicky, and any potential threat can cause a stampede.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.par: Parasaurolophus was a hadrosaur that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous. It measured 10 m long, and weighed about 2.5 tons. Its large, curved, tubular crest on its head was hollow, was used to produce sound. Parasaurolophus was a herbivore, and like other hadrosaurs, it used cheek teeth to grind its food. Parasaurolophus lives in herds of about 5 - 50 animals, a mix of males and females. Parasaur calls can travel for miles, and they are very loud.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.tri: Triceratops lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous. They were herbivorous, eating mainly palms, cycads and ferns. When fully grown, Triceratops measured 8-9 m long and weighed 6-12 tons. The head frill was used for display, while the horns were used for attack and defence. Triceratops lives in family groups of 5 - 15 individuals led by an adult female matriarch.
gui.jurassicraft.field_guide.species.tyr: Tyrannosaurus rex was a huge theropod that lived during the Late Cretaceous in North America. It grew about 12-13 metres long, and 6 tons in weight. Healed bite wounds from T. rex found on herbivore bones suggest that it was indeed a predator. However, it also scavenged. They led a violent lifestyle, and were fiercely territorial. T. rex is magnificent, but is not to be taken lightly!
gui.jurassicraft.dna_slot.extract_sample: Amber, sea lamprey or dinosaur meat
jei.jurassicraft.note.cleaning: One random result. A bucket of water supplies eight cleaning cycles and returns an empty bucket.
jei.jurassicraft.note.nest: One random result: 1-7 eggs (50%), flint (25%), or bone meal (25%). Water is also required.
jei.jurassicraft.note.bone: One random result: bone meal (50%), flint (33%), or tissue (17%). Tissue retains sample data.
jei.jurassicraft.note.egg: One random result: tissue from a random species (33%), bone meal (33%), or flint (33%).
jei.jurassicraft.note.plant_fossil: One random result: bone meal (50%), flint (25%), or tissue from a random species (25%).
jei.jurassicraft.note.sequence: Untagged samples get random genes and 5-100% quality in steps of five. Existing DNA is preserved.
jei.jurassicraft.note.random_dna: Species, DNA quality and animal genes are random; existing DNA is preserved.
jei.jurassicraft.note.meat: Extracts valid DNA from raw meat and preserves its species, quality and genes.
jei.jurassicraft.note.preserve: The genetic information on the input is preserved.
jei.jurassicraft.note.combine: Same species: qualities add up to 100%; the first disc's genes remain. Examples cycle independently.
jei.jurassicraft.note.synthesize: Requires 100% DNA. The disc is reusable; the test tube and nucleotides are consumed.
jei.jurassicraft.note.temperature: Consumes peat moss. Temperature at or below 50 gives a female; above 50 gives a male.
jei.jurassicraft.note.cultivate: Transfer adds the syringe only. Fill with two buckets of water and enough food for all four nutrients. Temperature determines sex.
jei.jurassicraft.note.skeleton: Arrange matching fossil or fresh bones in this pattern.
jei.jurassicraft.note.breeding: One food item produces the shown insects. The parent insect stays in the crate.
jei.jurassicraft.note.peat: Moss can spread naturally onto nearby exposed peat without consuming the original moss.
jei.jurassicraft.note.figure_cycle: Craft a figure by itself to cycle through dinosaur species. Other figure data is preserved.
